name: Enemy-role differentiation
summary: An enemy earns a roster slot when its readable behavior creates a distinct priority, positioning demand, resource decision, or interruption pattern.
player_action: The player identifies an enemy role, predicts its pressure, and changes target, position, timing, weapon, or resource use.
system_response: Silhouette, movement, sound, attack timing, range, vulnerability, and group behavior consistently expose the enemy's decision pressure.

conflicts_with: enemy variety expressed only through health and damage

failure_modes: Two enemy types produce the same optimal response.
The dangerous role is identifiable only after unavoidable damage.
Visual size or rarity implies a role the behavior does not perform.
One universal weapon and position dominate every role.
accessibility: Repeat role identity across silhouette, motion, sound, iconography, and attack rhythm.
Provide adjustable telegraph contrast without changing authoritative timing.

smallest_playable_test.setup: Four enemies with one role each: pursuer, area denial, support, and ranged punish; test alone, in pairs, and in mixed groups.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: Players can explain each role and mixed compositions change priority or movement without relying on labels.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: Roles are distinct in isolation but collapse into visual noise in groups.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: Removing an enemy type changes only total health, damage, or completion time.

evidence.claim: Bethesda presents id Software's enemy process around knowing distinct adversaries and learning how to defeat them.
evidence.notes: Supports enemy-specific counterknowledge; detailed role causality still requires playable comparison.
